hero.intro: I design and build the whole thing: the screens people touch, the APIs behind them and the dashboards that show whether any of it worked.

about.statement: I'm Rowan. I like the part of a project where a messy idea turns into something you can click.
paragraphs: Most of my work sits between design and engineering. I sketch the flow, build the interface, wire up the API and then watch the numbers to see what people actually do with it.
I keep stacks boring on purpose. TypeScript, Postgres and a good component library get most products to launch, and I save the clever bits for where they pay off.
about.caption: Lisbon, Portugal

build.aside: The four kinds of work I take on most, start to finish.

rows.title: Interfaces
rows.description: Design systems, product screens and the small interactions that make an app feel finished.

rows.title: APIs
rows.description: Typed, documented endpoints with auth, tests and logs, so the frontend never has to guess.

rows.title: Dashboards
rows.description: Charts and reports that answer one question each, built on data you can trust.

rows.title: Launches
rows.description: From a sketch to a live URL with analytics on day one, then small releases every week.

work.aside: Three example projects. Swap these for real ones: the build reads the same fields for any project.

projects.name: Driftmail
projects.tagline: A shared inbox that sorts itself.
projects.description: Support teams forward everything to one address. Driftmail reads each thread, tags it, routes it to the right person and drafts a reply they can send or edit.

media.alt: Driftmail banner: a shared inbox that sorts itself.
media.label: Banner

projects.name: Coinpath
projects.description: Connect a bank export and Coinpath groups the spending, flags what changed this month and writes a two-line summary you can read on the bus.

media.alt: Coinpath banner: budgets that explain themselves.

projects.name: Murmur
projects.tagline: Voice memos in, tidy notes out.
projects.description: Record a meeting on your phone. Murmur transcribes it on the device, pulls out decisions and to-dos and files them where your team already works.

media.alt: Murmur banner: voice memos in, tidy notes out.

sideQuests.name: Swatchbot
sideQuests.description: Drop in any screenshot and get a named, accessible colour palette back.
sideQuests.alt: Swatchbot banner with four tilted colour swatches.

sideQuests.name: Shelf
sideQuests.description: A reading log that lives in your terminal and syncs to a plain text file.
sideQuests.alt: Shelf banner with a row of books on a shelf.

archive.note: Every public repository, synced live from GitHub. (The example points at GitHub's demo account.)

stack.heading: Daily drivers.
stack.aside: Every tool in my rotation, in one pit. Grab one and throw it.

steps.title: Find the one job
steps.text: We agree on the single thing the first version has to do well, and what it can skip.

steps.title: Clickable in a week
steps.text: You get a working build on a real URL early, so feedback is about the product, not a mockup.

steps.title: Ship small, often
steps.text: Weekly releases with the numbers next to them, so every change earns its place.

contact.lede: Got a product idea, a rough prototype or a launch date coming up? Send it over. I reply within a day.
